'''Takeel''' was a [[Snivvian/Legends|Snivvian]] [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] and burned-out [[Spice/Legends|spice]] addict who frequented [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Cantina]], looking for employment. He was also known by the nickname "Hunchback".

==Biography==
Takeel and his brother were monitored from birth by Snivvian society due to the flaw in the [[Blood Code]] causing male [[Twin/Legends|twins]] to have a chance of one of the brothers developing psychopathic tendencies. When he started to walk and talk before his brother, he was subjected to personality reprogramming which left him with greatly reduced cognitive abilities.<ref name="AJ11" /> Takeel at times worked for [[Durga Besadii Tai]], [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]], and the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], and earned his reputation as a double-crosser from his habit of turning over lawbreakers (including former partners) to Imperial law enforcement.

In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], he was tasked by Jabba to find a missing droid, [[CZ-3/Legends|CZ-3]]<ref name="AJ11" />

Takeel was the brother of [[Zutton/Legends|Zutton]]. Like all Snivvians, he would sometimes be nicknamed "Snaggletooth" by other species.

{{Char-stub}}
==Behind the scenes==
A card from the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Customizable Card Game'']] titled "Hunchback" only shows Takeel from behind. The card reads "What hump?", probably a reference to a line from the film [[Wikipedia:Young Frankenstein|''Young Frankenstein'']].

Takeel can be seen in ''A New Hope'' with "human hands", as his actor wasn't given gloves or later-produced prosthetic Snivvian hands.

In Insider #130 - "The Unusual Suspects: Who's Who in Mos Eisley" there are discrepancies between the pictured [[Reegesk/Legends|Reegesk's]] mask and that seen in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]. The [[Ranat/Legends|Ranat]] pictured in this issue of Insider may in fact be [[Nevar Yalnal/Legends|Nevar Yalnal]] however this has yet to be clarified by [[Leland Chee]]. The confusion continues with both [[Takeel/Legends|Takeel]] and [[Zutton/Legends|Zutton]] reversed from their Decipher CCG images. In the Decipher cards [[Zutton/Legends|Zutton]] is shown with a full head of hair while in the Insider image he now has patchy hair and a large hump. Takeel is shown by Decipher to have patchy hair and a large hump but in the Insider image he is shown with a full head of hair and a small hump. The identified images of [[Mosep Binneed/Legends|Mosep Binneed]] and [[Tawss Khaa/Legends|Tawss Khaa]] also differ from those used by Decipher.
